description: Sample file. Replace the three questions below with your own; keep the shape.

sba.stem: A 28-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks' gestation has a blood pressure of 158/104 mmHg on two readings four hours apart, and a urine protein:creatinine ratio of 48 mg/mmol. She has no headache, visual disturbance or epigastric pain. Fetal growth is on the 40th centile with a normal umbilical artery Doppler.
sba.lead: What is the most appropriate first-line antihypertensive agent?
sba.rationale: Labetalol is first-line for hypertension in pregnancy. Nifedipine and methyldopa are alternatives where labetalol is contraindicated — asthma, for instance. Atenolol is associated with fetal growth restriction and is avoided.

sba.stem: A 32-year-old woman is seen six weeks after a normal vaginal delivery. She is breastfeeding exclusively and wants contraception.
sba.lead: Which method is LEAST appropriate at this visit?
sba.rationale: Combined hormonal contraception is UKMEC 4 under six weeks postpartum in a breastfeeding woman and UKMEC 2 from six weeks to six months. Progestogen-only methods and intrauterine methods are all suitable.
sba.hook: Breastfeeding + postpartum → avoid combined oestrogen early.

emq.instruction: For each woman below, select the SINGLE most likely diagnosis. Each option may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

stems.stem: A 30-year-old at 32 weeks has sudden painless bright red bleeding. The uterus is soft and non-tender; the fetal heart is normal. She had a lower-segment caesarean two years ago.
stems.rationale: Painless bleeding with a soft uterus and a normal fetal heart points to praevia; a previous caesarean is a risk factor.

stems.stem: A 36-year-old at 34 weeks has constant abdominal pain and dark vaginal bleeding. The uterus is woody-hard and tender, and the cardiotocograph shows late decelerations.
stems.rationale: Pain, a tense tender uterus and fetal compromise are the picture of abruption.

statements.stem: Proteinuria is required for the diagnosis.
statements.rationale: Since the 2018 ISSHP definition, hypertension with any maternal organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction is sufficient. Proteinuria is not mandatory.

statements.stem: Low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks reduces the risk in high-risk women.
statements.rationale: 150 mg at night from 12 weeks until delivery is recommended for women with one high risk factor or two moderate ones.

statements.stem: Delivery of the placenta is the definitive treatment.
statements.rationale: It is the only cure; everything else buys time or manages the complications.
